scripts.script: Thank you for the offer — I am excited about the role. For this role and experience band, indicative market data puts the median around the middle of the range, and my offer sits below the floor. Would you consider moving the base closer to the median? I am happy to discuss the full package.
scripts.tip: Name the median, not the maximum — it keeps the ask credible.
scripts.title: Anchor to the median

scripts.script: I appreciate the offer. If the base band is fixed, could we look at the joining bonus, the first review timeline, or learning support instead? I want to say yes — I just need the overall package to be closer to market.
scripts.tip: Ask what is flexible besides base pay.
scripts.title: Trade base for the full package

scripts.script: Thank you — I would like a day to review the details before I respond. After reviewing market ranges for this role, I believe a base near the median is fair given my skills, and I will share that reasoning in writing. Can we keep the offer open until then?
scripts.tip: Never accept on the spot when the number is low.
scripts.title: Buy time, then counter in writing

scripts.script: The base looks fair against market ranges. Before I accept, could you confirm the breakup in writing — fixed versus variable, joining bonus, and the first appraisal cycle? Once that is clear, I am ready to decide quickly.
scripts.tip: Confirm the breakup in writing before accepting.
scripts.title: Confirm the full breakup

scripts.script: I am happy with the base. Would there be flexibility on a joining bonus or an early performance review at six months? One of those would make this an easy yes for me.
scripts.tip: Small, specific asks work best at the median.
scripts.title: Ask for one meaningful extra

scripts.script: The offer is competitive. Could we agree on a six-month review with clear goals tied to a raise, and confirm the role title? Growth velocity matters as much to me as the starting number.
scripts.tip: Titles and growth compound over a career.
scripts.title: Negotiate growth, not just pay

scripts.script: Thank you — this is a strong offer and I am glad to accept. Could you confirm the joining date, the pay breakup, and the review cycle in writing so I can plan my transition? I look forward to joining the team.
scripts.tip: Strong offers deserve a fast, gracious yes.
scripts.title: Accept graciously, confirm details

scripts.script: This offer is above the indicative market range for the role, so I do not want to haggle over the base. If there is a small joining bonus or relocation support available, I would appreciate it — otherwise I am happy to accept as offered.
scripts.tip: Do not push a strong offer into a rescinded one.
scripts.title: Do not over-negotiate a win

scripts.script: The total looks excellent. Could you break down how much is fixed, how much is variable, and what the variable payout depends on? I want to understand the guaranteed portion before I sign.
scripts.tip: Clarify variable pay before celebrating the total.
scripts.title: Check what the headline really pays

scripts.script: I have another offer at a higher number, and I prefer your team. Can you match it or close the gap? I can decide by the end of the week, and I will be transparent about my timeline.
scripts.tip: Only mention an offer you actually hold.
scripts.title: Use the better offer as data

scripts.script: I am comparing two offers and yours is my first choice on team and work. The other offer is higher on base — is there room to move, or to add a joining bonus? I will not share the other letter, but I can confirm the number verbally.
scripts.tip: Never share the other offer letter.
scripts.title: Keep the other offer private

scripts.script: I understand fresher bands are often fixed, and I am grateful for the offer. Could we agree on a six-month performance review with a raise linked to clear goals? That gives me a path to market quickly.
scripts.tip: Freshers gain more from reviews than from one-time bumps.
scripts.title: First offer: negotiate the review

scripts.script: This is my first offer, so I am weighing the team, the learning, and the growth path alongside pay. If the base cannot move, could we discuss mentorship, the first project, or a joining bonus? Those matter a lot for my first year.
scripts.tip: Do not reject a first offer over a small gap.
scripts.title: First offer: weigh the whole launchpad

scripts.script: During my internship I shipped work the team relies on, and I would love to convert. What does the PPO band look like for converting interns at my level, and how is it set? I want to make sure the conversion reflects my contribution.
scripts.tip: Cite shipped work, not hours spent.
scripts.title: Convert on shipped work

scripts.script: I am excited to convert. Before I accept, could you share the band and the review timeline for the converted role? I want to compare it with indicative market ranges so I join with confidence, not doubts.
scripts.tip: Verify the PPO against market before assuming it is fair.
scripts.title: Verify the PPO band
